mission_10: Congratulations on completing the Speech Recognition chapter! You have now built a comprehensive multilingual speech recognition system that handles multiple languages, detects code-switching, and evaluates performance across languages. The language embedding approach enables a single model to adapt its behavior for different languages by conditioning the encoder and decoder on language identity, dramatically reducing the deployment cost compared to maintaining separate models. The self-attention encoder captures long-range dependencies in the audio signal while incorporating language-specific biases through the added language embeddings. Code-switching detection identifies language boundaries by comparing the acoustic characteristics of adjacent windows against language-specific centroids, enabling the system to handle the natural language mixing that occurs in multilingual communities. The multilingual decoder generates text using language-specific vocabulary mappings while sharing the core architecture across all languages. Per-language WER evaluation ensures that the model maintains quality across all supported languages, preventing the common pitfall where high-resource languages dominate the training signal. Together with the nine previous missions covering MFCC features, wav2vec 2.0, CTC loss, Whisper architecture, speaker diarization, noise robustness, streaming ASR, keyword spotting, and end-to-end ASR, you now possess a complete understanding of modern speech recognition from classical signal processing to cutting-edge deep learning architectures.
